subject: mathematics
question_text: If i, j, k are unit vectors along the positive directions of the coordinate axes, then show that the four points 4i+5j+k, −j−k, 3i+9j+4k and −4i+4j+4k are coplanar.

mark_split.label: Conclude that the points are coplanar

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.58 — SAQ chapter 8 Addition of Vectors, answer 49.1. recall_prompt: Say how you would show four points are coplanar — say what vectors you build first and what test you apply to them.

steps.label: Write the position vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the four points P, Q, R, S and take O as the origin. The names are what let every later line stay short.
steps.memory_tip: Name the points P, Q, R, S with O as the origin. i, j, k are automatically non-coplanar.

recall.must_convey: That the four given vectors are named as the position vectors OP, OQ, OR, OS of four points P, Q, R, S, measured from an origin O.
accept: call the four position vectors OP OQ OR OS with O as the origin
name the four points P Q R S and write their position vectors from O
take the given vectors as position vectors of four points from the origin
naalugu points ni P Q R S ani peru petti, O origin ga teeskuntam
let the four given vectors be the position vectors of P Q R and S

steps.why: A position vector is measured from the origin; the vector BETWEEN two points is the difference of their position vectors. Setting the origin up front is what makes that subtraction legal.
common_mistakes: Treating the given vectors as the sides of the figure rather than as positions.
Never naming an origin, so the differences below have nothing to be measured from.

steps.label: Find PQ, PR and PS
steps.margin_note: Second mark. All three vectors must start at the SAME point — P here. Three edges from one corner is what makes them testable for coplanarity; three edges picked at random is not. i, j, k are non-coplanar by definition — they point along three different axes — so the same test applies, and here the determinant IS the scalar triple product with no [a b c] factor left over.
steps.memory_tip: All three from P. With i, j, k there is no [a b c] factor to carry.

recall.must_convey: That PQ, PR and PS are found by subtracting OP from each of the other three position vectors — all three starting from the same point P.
accept: find PQ PR and PS by subtracting OP from OQ OR and OS so all three start at P
each edge vector is the far position vector minus OP
take the differences from the same point P to get three vectors
OQ minus OP, OR minus OP, OS minus OP — anni P nunchi start avthai
subtract the first position vector from the other three

steps.why: Four points are coplanar exactly when three vectors joining ONE of them to the other three lie in a plane. Anchoring all three at P is not a convention — it is the condition.
common_mistakes: Building PQ, QR and RS, a chain rather than three edges from one corner.
Subtracting the wrong way round; OQ − OP, not OP − OQ.
A sign slip when the subtracted term is already negative.

steps.label: Evaluate the determinant
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Write the three vectors as the rows of a determinant, in order, and expand along the top row. Three vectors lie in a plane exactly when this comes out 0.
steps.memory_tip: Rows of a determinant, expanded along the top row. Zero means coplanar.

recall.must_convey: That the three vectors are put in as the rows of a determinant — the scalar triple product — and that it evaluates to 0.
accept: put the three vectors as rows of a determinant, the scalar triple product, and it comes out zero
take the box product of PQ PR PS and expand the determinant to get zero
the scalar triple product is a three by three determinant and it is zero here
moodu vectors ni determinant rows ga rasi expand cheste zero vasthundi
evaluate the triple product determinant and it equals zero

steps.why: The scalar triple product is the volume of the box the three vectors span. Zero volume means the box is flat — which is exactly what it means for three vectors to lie in one plane.
common_mistakes: Getting the sign pattern wrong when expanding: plus, minus, plus along the top row.
Putting the vectors in as columns and rows inconsistently.
Omitting a zero coefficient and shifting the whole row.

steps.label: Conclude coplanar
steps.margin_note: Last mark, and it is two statements, not one: the VECTORS are coplanar, therefore the POINTS are. Stopping at the vectors leaves the question half answered.
steps.memory_tip: The vectors are coplanar, therefore the points are. Write both.
lines: So PQ, PR, PS are coplanar.

lines.text: ∴ The four points P, Q, R, S are coplanar.

recall.must_convey: That a zero scalar triple product makes the three vectors coplanar, and therefore the four points are coplanar.
accept: since the triple product is zero the three vectors are coplanar so the four points are coplanar
zero means the vectors lie in a plane and so do the four points
the vectors are coplanar hence the points P Q R S are coplanar
triple product zero kabatti vectors coplanar, so naalugu points kuda coplanar
therefore the four given points lie in one plane

steps.why: The three vectors all start at P, so if they lie in a plane that plane also contains P — and with it Q, R and S. That last sentence is what turns a fact about vectors into the answer about points.
common_mistakes: Writing only that the vectors are coplanar and never mentioning the points.
